subject: NeoPort hosted API — monthly consumption envelope + peak concurrency confirmation
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neoport.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@neoport.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NeoPort hosted API — monthly consumption envelope + peak concurrency confirmation

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and the asks I promised to put in writing so we can align with procurement/finance on the next steps. TL;DR: you indicated a midline monthly token envelope and a short daily peak window; for pricing we discussed committed bands vs burst capacity. Please confirm or correct the bullets below.

Summary (your inputs from today)
- Expected steady monthly token consumption: "~160M - 220M tokens / month" (you mentioned growth from POC to production in Q4).
- Peak concurrency: 99th-percentile concurrent TPS observed during busiest minute: "~1,200 TPS" (peaks are concentrated in a 10–30 minute window, not sustained).
- Typical request size: ~850 tokens per request (avg across chat + moderate history).
- Budget guidance: NeoPort finance indicated a target cost band of "$12k–$20k / month" initially; you asked for unit $/1M to map against internal targets.

What Redwood proposes for next steps
1) Confirm the monthly envelope and 99th TPS above (or give corrected ranges).
2) Share the attached forecast spreadsheet with 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / stretch) — please add any missing columns and return it so we can wire up pricing bands. (attached: NeoPort_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx)
3) If the expected envelope is in the 160–220M range, we can present a committed band proposal that targets ~$14–$16 per 1M tokens (tiered by commit) and a burst add-on for peak windows. Final unit pricing depends on average tokens / request and prefix caching eligibility.
4) If this works, we can push a short pilot PO (30–60 days) to lock in a temporary committed rate while you run performance validation. I can loop in Karthik for an official pricing model and a DocuSign pilot PO when you sign off.

Open questions for NeoPort
- Can you confirm peak window duration (is it 10, 20 or 30 minutes typical)?
- Are any flows latency-sensitive (<200ms target) that we need to account for in routing/capacity?
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency) for primary traffic?

Thanks — I’ve cc'd Priya for anything I missed and will loop in Karthik/marissa on the pricing side once you confirm.

— Grace O'Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachment: NeoPort_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub; columns: month, scenario, avg_tokens_per_request, est_monthly_tokens, peak_99_tps, notes)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@neoport.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@neoport.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeoPort hosted API — monthly consumption envelope + peak concurrency confirmation

Grace — thanks for the clear notes. Mostly accurate; a few clarifications/edits below.

Corrections / confirmations
- Monthly envelope: lean toward the higher side of the range based on roadmap: we expect "180M - 240M tokens / month" in steady state after Q4 ramp. Q4 POC expected ~60–80M for the first 30 days.
- Peak concurrency: confirm 99th pctl ~"1,300 TPS" during business-hours spike (we have multiple regions but primary traffic is US-east). Peaks are more like 15–20 minute windows during batch runs plus a smaller afternoon spike.
- Avg tokens / request: revise to "~720 tokens" after we trim prompt history for production.
- Budget: finance gave rough target of "$15k–$25k / month" — willing to consider committed pricing if there’s predictability.

Two additional notes
- We will be using short-term prefix caching for a subset of 30% of requests (templated responses), which will lower effective billable tokens.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 is required; we'll need the standard security questionnaire and a copy of the SLA.

I filled the conservative/expected/stretch tabs in the attached forecast and added Q4 ramp assumptions. See attached: NeoPort_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (updated).

If you can share the committed-band pricing scenarios (per 1M tokens) and the burst pricing model for peak TPS, we can route for internal signoff. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up next week if it helps.

— Alex
Head of Product | NeoPort
alex.turner@neoport.ai | +1 617-555-0124

Attachment: NeoPort_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (updated; includes Q4 ramp and prefix caching %)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: FWD: NeoPort hosted API — monthly consumption envelope + peak concurrency confirmation

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Alex's confirmation. Key inputs for pricing model: expected steady state 180M–240M tokens / month, 99th pctl peak ~1,300 TPS (15–20 min windows), avg tokens/request ~720, ~30% prefix-cacheable. Finance target ~$15k–$25k/month.

Can you:
- Draft two committed-band options (6-month pilot and 12-month commit) showing unit $/1M, expected monthly bill at midline and stretch, and an explicit burst add-on for peak TPS windows?
- Include notes on how prefix caching impacts effective billable tokens (assume 30% reduction on eligible traffic) and any latency SLO tradeoffs if we pin to cheaper variants.
- Attach a short one-pager with the pilot PO language we typically use (DocuSign link staged).

I attached the NeoPort forecast they returned. Please keep Alex + Priya on the thread for transparency.

Thanks — Grace

Attachment: NeoPort_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@neoport.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Desai <priya@neoport.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NeoPort hosted API — monthly consumption envelope + peak concurrency confirmation

Alex / Grace / Priya — attached is a short pricing summary and two committed-band proposals plus a pilot PO option. High-level highlights below; full numbers in the attached PDF.

Proposed committed bands (illustrative)
- Pilot (30–60 day): 1) Midline commit 100M tokens => $16.5 per 1M (effective monthly: $1,650) — used for verification and to secure baseline capacity.
- 6-month commit: 180M/month commit => $14.5 per 1M (midline monthly bill ~$2,610). Stretch band 240M => $13.2 per 1M.
- 12-month commit: 180M/month => $13.2 per 1M; 240M/month => $12.0 per 1M (volume discounts apply).

Burst / peak windows
- For the 15–20 minute 99th pctl windows (1,300 TPS), we recommend a burst pool priced as a short-term capacity add-on: $0.40 per 1,000 tokens consumed during burst minutes (applied only to tokens beyond committed bucket). This keeps committed $/1M attractive while covering transient capacity.

Prefix caching impact
- With ~30% prefix-cacheable traffic, effective billable tokens reduce ~20–25% overall (depends on distribution). We model that into the committed bands — final numbers will adjust after they return the forecast with the cacheable-tagged traffic column.

SLA / compliance
- We can provide SOC 2 attestation and SLA draft (attached: redwood_pricing-bands_v1.pdf).

Next steps
1) Alex/Priya: confirm you accept the high-level bands above and decide whether you want a 6- or 12-month pricing pilot.
2) If yes, I’ll drop a DocuSign pilot PO and a short SOW (30–60 days) for testing; we’ll lock the midline rate while you run perf validation.

DocuSign pilot PO: https://www.docusign.com/neoport/pilot-po-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/NP-2026-009

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Pricing Manager | Redwood Inference
